title: Turkey
eyebrow: Two continents, many ways to travel
summary: Istanbul energy, Cappadocian valleys, and Aegean and Mediterranean coastlines in one rich destination.
overview: Turkey gives a journey room to change pace: move from Bosphorus-facing neighborhoods and historic architecture in Istanbul to Cappadocia's volcanic valleys, then toward coastal towns and archaeological sites. Food, design, and a deep sense of history keep the route grounded.

highlights.title: Istanbul
highlights.description: Move between historic quarters, Bosphorus views, museums, markets, and the everyday energy of a city linking Europe and Asia.
highlights.alt: Istanbul skyline with mosque domes and the Bosphorus

highlights.title: Cappadocia
highlights.description: Explore a distinctive landscape of fairy chimneys, valleys, cave spaces, and villages shaped by volcanic stone.
highlights.alt: Hot air balloons over Cappadocia at sunrise

highlights.title: Aegean and Mediterranean coast
highlights.description: Follow the shores for coastal towns, clear water, and archaeological traces beside the sea.

experiences.title: City stories
experiences.description: Let Istanbul set the pace with architecture, food, neighborhoods, and views across the Bosphorus.

experiences.title: Volcanic landscapes
experiences.description: Make space for Cappadocia's valleys, stone formations, and quiet early-morning light.

experiences.title: Coastal discovery
experiences.description: Balance cultural depth with relaxed days along the Aegean and Mediterranean shores.

bestTimeToVisit: For city walks and inland discovery, many travelers prefer spring or autumn. Summer is popular for coastal stays, while Cappadocia's highland setting can feel cooler than the shoreline.

usefulInformation.label: Language
usefulInformation.value: Turkish; English is common in major visitor areas.

usefulInformation.label: Currency
usefulInformation.value: Turkish lira.

usefulInformation.label: Travel character
usefulInformation.value: A varied destination combining urban culture, heritage, nature, and coast.

usefulInformation.label: Planning note
usefulInformation.value: Distances between regions are meaningful, so a thoughtful route makes the experience easier.

title: Russia
summary: Moscow and Saint Petersburg meet in a culture-led route of grand architecture, museums, and waterways.
overview: A Russia journey can move between Moscow's historic centre and Saint Petersburg's canal-lined urban landscape. The focus is cultural: public squares, museums, theatres, palaces, and the architectural details that give each city its own rhythm.

highlights.title: Moscow
highlights.description: Discover the Kremlin and Red Square at the historic heart of the capital, then continue through museums, galleries, and lively neighborhoods.
highlights.alt: Colorful architecture in Moscow at blue hour

highlights.title: Saint Petersburg
highlights.description: Follow canals, embankments, grand ensembles, and the cultural institutions of Russia's northern capital.
highlights.alt: Historic architecture beside water in Saint Petersburg

highlights.title: Museums and heritage
highlights.description: Build time around art, architecture, music, and historic spaces so the cities are experienced rather than rushed.

experiences.title: Historic city centres
experiences.description: Take in the scale of Moscow and Saint Petersburg through their squares, streets, monuments, and waterways.

experiences.title: A museum-led journey
experiences.description: Leave room for the museums and collections that give each city its cultural texture.

experiences.title: Architecture in changing light
experiences.description: Notice how morning, evening, and winter light change the character of great facades and public spaces.

bestTimeToVisit: The most suitable season depends on the route and experience you want. Warmer months support long city walks and riverfront time, while winter brings a different atmosphere and requires more careful planning for weather.

title: Bali
eyebrow: An island with its own rhythm
summary: Ubud's rice landscapes, temple traditions, and coastlines create a slower island rhythm.
overview: Bali is a distinct island destination with its own cultural and natural character. Move from Ubud's rice landscapes and creative life to temple settings, beaches, and time outdoors, leaving enough space for both discovery and pause.

highlights.title: Ubud
highlights.description: Spend time among galleries, craft traditions, rice-field landscapes, and the cultural energy of central Bali.
highlights.alt: Balinese temple surrounded by tropical greenery

highlights.title: Temple landscapes
highlights.description: Take in temple architecture, carved details, and the cultural traditions that shape the island's daily rhythm.

highlights.title: Beaches and coastlines
highlights.description: Choose a coastal rhythm that matches you, from sunrise walks to lively surf beaches and quieter shores.

experiences.title: Culture in motion
experiences.description: Let ceremonies, dance, craft, and architecture add meaning to the places you visit.

experiences.title: Green escapes
experiences.description: Move inland for rice terraces, forest paths, and the slower pace of Ubud and its surroundings.

experiences.title: A day by the sea
experiences.description: Keep the route open for swimming, sunsets, and the coastal pace that suits you.

bestTimeToVisit: The drier months are generally popular for outdoor plans, while the wetter season can bring lush landscapes and shorter, more flexible outings. Local conditions vary across the island and by activity.

title: Georgia
eyebrow: Cities, mountains, and the shared table
summary: Tbilisi streets, Caucasus horizons, Kakheti tables, and a culture shaped by many crossroads.
overview: Georgia brings together Tbilisi's layered streets, the high landscapes around Kazbegi, Kakheti's food and wine traditions, and the different character of the country's regions. The appeal is in the contrast between city, mountain, table, and road.

highlights.title: Tbilisi
highlights.description: Wander through a capital where historic streets, bath districts, balconies, and contemporary creative life sit side by side.

highlights.title: Kazbegi and the Caucasus
highlights.description: Head north for wide mountain views, high valleys, and villages where the landscape becomes the main story.

highlights.title: Kakheti and the table
highlights.description: Make space for regional food, village hospitality, and the long relationship between Georgia, vineyards, and the shared table.

experiences.title: A city with layers
experiences.description: Use Tbilisi as a starting point for architecture, baths, food, and a growing contemporary scene.

experiences.title: Mountain air
experiences.description: Trade the city for the Caucasus when you want wide views, walking, and a stronger sense of distance.

experiences.title: Food, wine, and place
experiences.description: Let regional cuisine, vineyards, and the shared table become part of how you understand the country.

bestTimeToVisit: Georgia spans several landscapes and climates, so the best period depends on your route. Spring and autumn are inviting for cities, food, and walking; summer opens more mountain routes, while winter suits snow experiences in selected regions.

usefulInformation.label: Language
usefulInformation.value: Georgian; English is increasingly common in visitor-facing areas.

usefulInformation.label: Currency
usefulInformation.value: Georgian lari.

usefulInformation.label: Travel character
usefulInformation.value: A culturally rich crossroads blending cities, mountains, food, wine, and coast.

usefulInformation.label: Planning note
usefulInformation.value: Regional travel adds variety, but routes should allow for changing terrain and road times.

title: Indonesia
summary: Go beyond Bali through Java's heritage, volcanic landscapes, and the changing rhythms of a vast archipelago.
overview: Indonesia is a broad archipelago rather than a single travel style. Look to Java for Yogyakarta, heritage, and volcanic landscapes, then consider islands such as Lombok for a different balance of coastline, local culture, and open space. Bali remains its own distinct destination on this site.

highlights.title: Yogyakarta and Java
highlights.description: Discover a cultural centre shaped by palaces, crafts, living traditions, and the temple landscapes of Central Java.
highlights.alt: Stone temple surrounded by lush Indonesian forest

highlights.title: Volcanic landscapes
highlights.description: Java's geography adds a dramatic natural dimension, from highland views to the fertile landscapes shaped by volcanoes.

highlights.title: Lombok and beyond
highlights.description: Look toward Lombok and other regions for a different balance of coastline, local culture, and open space.

experiences.title: Living culture
experiences.description: Spend time with the traditions, crafts, food, and everyday scenes that make each region distinct.

experiences.title: Heritage and place
experiences.description: Use Yogyakarta and Central Java as a gateway to stories preserved in temples, palaces, and craft communities.

experiences.title: Island contrasts
experiences.description: Balance cultural discovery with the quieter pace of another island when the route allows.

bestTimeToVisit: Indonesia's scale means weather varies by island and activity. Drier months are often preferred for outdoor routes, but the best timing should be matched to the specific islands and experiences you want to include.

usefulInformation.label: Language
usefulInformation.value: Indonesian, alongside many regional languages; English is common in established visitor areas.

usefulInformation.label: Currency
usefulInformation.value: Indonesian rupiah.

usefulInformation.label: Travel character
usefulInformation.value: A diverse archipelago where culture, nature, heritage, and island life change across regions.

usefulInformation.label: Planning note
usefulInformation.value: Treat Indonesia as a multi-region destination and plan transfers with generous space.

title: Thailand
regionOrCity: Bangkok, Chiang Mai and the islands
eyebrow: City energy, northern calm, sea air
summary: Bangkok energy, Chiang Mai's northern character, and island coastlines in one flexible journey.
overview: Thailand works through contrast: Bangkok's river, temples, markets, and food; Chiang Mai's northern cultural character and mountain setting; and the coastlines around Phuket and other islands. The route can be as lively or unhurried as the balance you choose.

highlights.title: Bangkok
highlights.description: Take in the capital's temples, river life, markets, neighbourhoods, food, and bold modern energy.
highlights.alt: Golden temple roof in Bangkok at sunset

highlights.title: Chiang Mai
highlights.description: Explore a northern city where Lanna culture, creative streets, markets, and mountain nature meet.
highlights.alt: Temple and mountain landscape in Thailand

highlights.title: Islands and beaches
highlights.description: Slow the pace with a coastal stay shaped by warm water, boat days, and the kind of rest you are looking for.
highlights.alt: Blue tropical sea and sandy beach

experiences.title: City flavour
experiences.description: Let Bangkok's food, river, markets, and neighbourhoods introduce you to the country's energy.

experiences.title: Northern calm
experiences.description: Make room for Chiang Mai's cultural life and the natural spaces beyond the city.

experiences.title: Sea-change days
experiences.description: Add island time when you want the journey to open out into sun, water, and rest.

bestTimeToVisit: Thailand varies by region and coast, with seasonal differences that matter for city, mountain, and island plans. A route should be timed around the specific regions you want rather than one nationwide season assumption.
